body.statement:
For the saturated likelihood-ratio domain \(\mathcal V_P\), the full fixed-defect separated stratum \(\mathcal U_P\), and the actual path class in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{joint}}(P)\), does every \(s\in\mathcal C_P^\perp\) lie in the \(L^2(P)\)-closure of finite linear combinations of scores of admissible DQM paths, including at intersections with moving kernels and a shared \((W,X)\) marginal? Equivalently, does
\[
\mathcal T_P=\mathcal C_P^\perp
\]
hold on every such joint solvability germ?  Neither equality nor bridge-solvability path realization is included in the chart definition.
body.justification: This remains the reverse-inclusion problem for the full saturated fixed-defect intersection, not for an analyst-selected subchart.
body.gap: The finite constant-rank and branch calculations do not provide a general coupled Hilbert-space incidence chart, and operator continuity alone supplies no differentiable path lift.
body.consumer: Its resolution determines whether the affine projection is the information bound throughout the unrestricted joint model.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct actual DQM paths whose scores densely span the annihilator of the outcome-solvability, treatment-solvability, and null-space-interaction normals on the full saturated fixed-defect joint-solvability germ, or exhibit a counterexample within that same germ.
obligation.obstruction: For the coupled nuisance \(\eta=(h_0,h_1,q_0,q_1)\), the frozen assumptions give only continuous transported operators and kernel projections. They do not establish the local product-parameter attainability or bounded-direction density required by the analogues of Chen--Santos Assumptions 4.1(iv)--(v), nor a locally onto chart for the common-law incidence map with its shared \((W,X)\) marginal.
obligation.attempted: I linearized the four residual components \(g_a-T_ah_a\) and \(1-T_a^*q_a\), quotiented nuisance directions by the two kernels, and checked the available perturbation result along DQM paths. It yields only \(o(1)\) motion of kernel projectors, not the first-order lifts needed to integrate an arbitrary element of \(\mathcal C_P^\perp\). The three positive finite germs verify the construction only in their certified finite incidence charts.
obligation.partial_result:
The finite-dimensional calculations establish reverse lifting on the regular \(36\)-cell rank-two germ, the singular two-branch \(3\)-by-\(3\) germ, and the transverse \(4\)-by-\(4\) rank-two germ with different arm row spaces.  For the unrestricted Hilbert germ, DQM and the frozen perturbation lemma yield only
\[
 \|\widetilde\Pi_{N,a}(P_t)-\widetilde\Pi_{N,a}(P)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \vee
 \|\widetilde\Pi_{K,a}(P_t)-\widetilde\Pi_{K,a}(P)\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o(1).
\]
They provide neither an \(O(|t|)\) modulus nor a differentiable, locally onto chart for the coupled incidence map
\[
 (P',h_0,h_1,q_0,q_1)\longmapsto
 \bigl(g_a(P')-T_a(P')h_a,\ 1-T_a(P')^*q_a\bigr)_{a=0,1}
\]
after quotienting nuisance directions by \(\mathcal N_a(P)\) and \(\mathcal K_a(P)\).  Thus the analogues of Chen--Santos Assumptions 4.1(iv)--(v), especially attainability of bounded product directions and their density in \(\mathcal C_P^\perp\), are not consequences of the frozen primitives.
